A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 17 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original agent-training experiments, artificial-language evaluations and analyses of Spanish and Arabic inflectional sublanguages in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports additional inflection configurations in Table 3 and Appendix J.

M1.justification: The GRU agents, REINFORCE/backpropagation training, root weighting, HAS/BPE segmentation and articulation loss are retained. Implementation and loss descriptions move from v1 Appendices F/H to v2 A/I. Additional attribute configurations do not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds 42×2×2×2 and 42×6 inflection scenarios, changing the grammatical attributes that must be communicated, with corresponding natural-language comparisons. The reconstruction task and Spanish/Arabic sources remain; Appendix J explicitly reports that an Arabic reference was unavailable for 42×6.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain HAS, BPE96/BPEMax and the existing artificial, random and natural-language references. The added configurations reuse existing comparison methods; newly cited related work is not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: Previously both principal configurations had three attributes. The added experiments vary the attribute count across two, three and four while maintaining approximately 47–48 distinct values and testing both articulation conditions. Existing architecture, vocabulary, message length and metric settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The additional configurations support new sensitivity analyses of how grammatical attribute structure affects fusion and the TopSim response to articulation pressure. Earlier mutation, segmentation, ease-of-learning and failed-convergence analyses remain after appendix relocation.

E5.justification: v2 Table 3 adds ± uncertainty summaries for retained EmCom conditions previously reported as point estimates in v1 Table 7. Eight random initializations remain specified. The fusion-related t-test reported in v1 Appendix J is no longer reported.

E6.justification: From v1 Table 7 to v2 Table 3, unpressured default F-TopSim delta changes from 0.0112 to -0.0418, and unpressured 42×2×3 BPE BoSDis ratio changes from 45.4 to 1.23. Four condition rows and additional metric columns are added. The quantified Spanish fusion breakdown is removed. New Figure 11 also conflicts with Figure 5 on the retained 42×2×3 TopSim ordering.

T1.justification: The formal game specification, metric definitions and Equations 1–3 are retained, including relocated appendix equations. The new learnability paragraph restates the 99% accuracy criterion already specified in v1 Table 1; no substantive mathematical development is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the main contributions: small-vocabulary emergent morphology, concatenativity and fusion metrics, articulation pressure encouraging concatenation, and preferential grammatical-feature fusion resembling natural language.

C2.justification: Fusion interpretation changes substantially: v1 describes high fusion in the unpressured default setting and proposes that articulation suppresses fusion; v2 describes the default as least fusional and emphasizes 42×2×2×2 fusion. It drops the Spanish verb-class explanation, broadens claimed natural-language agreement, and adds configuration-dependent TopSim interpretation and a limitation concerning ground-truth inputs bypassing perception.

D1.justification: New Appendix K supplies resource links for EGG and both datasets, plus EGG and Spanish-dataset licensing information. Existing hardware, training and implementation details are retained after relocation. The explicit 683×2×3 specification of the failed control experiment disappears, although its description remains.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Chaabouni et al. (2022) on scaled, naturalistic visual communication and Kouwenhoven et al. (2024) on representational alignment, and expands its description of Conklin and Smith (2023). The central positioning relative to morphology and small-vocabulary EmCom research remains.

P1.justification: Main-text explanations are extensively tightened and rewritten, especially related work, metric descriptions and experimental reporting. Section 6 separates design from results, appendices are substantially reordered, fusion terminology is standardized, and the acknowledgements are removed.

P2.justification: The appendix experiment summary becomes an expanded main-text Table 3 with additional rows, columns and uncertainty displays. New Figures 10–11 provide substantial multi-panel comparisons across configurations. Existing Figures 1–9 largely retain their content but undergo relocation or resizing.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful configuration comparisons, uncertainty reporting, clearer limitations and resource information. However, its new Figure 11 contradicts retained Figure 5 and Table 3 on 42×2×3 TopSim, and it replaces v1's quantified Spanish fusion exception with an unquantified broader claim. These unresolved reporting inconsistencies undermine the added evidence, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
